tools.name: search_metadata
tools.description: Keyword-based search for data assets in OpenMetadata. Best when you know specific names, owners, tags, tiers, services, or column names. Use this for exact lookups (e.g., 'find table X', 'tables owned by team Y'), filtering by metadata properties, counting assets, and aggregations. Supports pagination and advanced OpenSearch DSL queries. Choose this over semantic_search when the query targets known identifiers or structured attributes. Results include 'fullyQualifiedName' and 'entityType' — pass these directly to get_entity_details for full entity information.

parameters.description: Use 'query' for keyword search or 'queryFilter' for advanced OpenSearch DSL. Best for exact matches and filtering by metadata properties.

query.description: Natural language search query. Use this for simple searches. Examples: 'tables owned by marketing', 'dashboards with customer data', 'tier1 tables', 'tables with column SKU', 'BigQuery services'. The query will be automatically converted to an optimized search.

entityType.description: Filter by entity type (auto-detected if not specified). Use singular form: table, dashboard, topic, pipeline, database, databaseService, glossary, glossaryTerm, mlmodel, container, chart, metric, user, team, domain, dataProduct.

queryFilter.description: Advanced: Direct OpenSearch JSON query string for precise control. Only use if you can generate valid OpenSearch DSL. When provided, this overrides the 'query' parameter. Must include entityType filter. Example: '{"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"entityType": "table"}}, {"nested": {"path": "owners", "query": {"term": {"owners.name": "marketing"}}}}]}}'. Key rules: Use singular entityType, 'owners.name' (plural), tier format is 'Tier.Tier1', columns are NOT nested, owners IS nested (wrap owners queries in {"nested": {"path": "owners", "query": ...}}).

from.description: In case the request more than 'size' results, this is the offset from the first result you want to fetch. Default is 0.

size.description: Number of results to return. Default is 10, we can iteratively page through results by increasing 'from'. Maximum allowed is 50.

includeDeleted.description: Include deleted entities in search results. Default is false.

fields.description:
Comma-separated additional fields to include. Default returns: name, displayName, fullyQualifiedName, description, entityType, service, database, databaseSchema, serviceType, href, tags, owners, tier, tableType, columnNames.

Additional fields by entity type:
- Table entities: columns, schemaDefinition, queries, upstreamLineage, entityRelationship
- Topic entities: messageSchema, partitions, replicationFactor  
- Dashboard entities: charts, dataModels, project
- Pipeline entities: tasks, pipelineUrl, scheduleInterval
- All entities: createdAt, updatedAt, changeDescription, extension, domain, dataProducts, lifeCycle, sourceHash

Example: 'columns,queries' for table column details and sample queries.

includeAggregations.description: Whether to include aggregation data (facets) in the response. Defaults to false to optimize LLM context size. Set to true only when you need aggregation statistics like counts by service type, owner, tags, etc. Aggregations can significantly increase response size.

maxAggregationBuckets.description: Maximum number of aggregation buckets to return per field when includeAggregations is true. Limits response size to prevent context overflow. Default is 10, maximum allowed is 50.

examples.description: Simple search - Find tables owned by a team
Simple search - Find customer-related data
Search with pagination (envelope response includes pagination block)
Simple search - Find tier1 tables
Simple search - Find dashboards
Advanced - Owner filter with OpenSearch
Advanced - Column search with OpenSearch
Advanced - Tier1 tables with OpenSearch
Advanced - Tag filtering with OpenSearch
Advanced - Aggregation query for counting

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Meaning-based discovery of data assets using vector embeddings. Best for exploratory or vague queries where you don't know exact names — it finds conceptually related assets even when no keywords match. Use this when the user describes what data they need in plain language (e.g., 'tables about customer spending behavior', 'anything related to revenue forecasting'). Returns entity summaries in a structured envelope with pagination and warnings (e.g. ignored filters). Results include 'fullyQualifiedName' and 'entityType' — pass these directly to get_entity_details for full entity information. Choose this over search_metadata when the query is about meaning or concepts rather than specific identifiers or attributes.

parameters.description: Use 'query' to describe what you're looking for in plain language. The system finds conceptually similar assets using vector similarity. Optionally filter by entity type, service, or tags.

query.description: Natural language query describing what you're looking for. Semantic search finds conceptually similar results, so phrasing matters more than exact keywords. Examples: 'customer purchase history', 'tables tracking revenue metrics', 'pipeline processing user events'.

filters.description: Optional filters to narrow results. Keys are field names and values are arrays of allowed values. Supported filter fields: 'entityType' (e.g., ['table', 'dashboard']), 'service' (e.g., ['BigQuery', 'Snowflake']), 'tags' (e.g., ['PII.Sensitive']). Example: {"entityType": ["table"], "service": ["BigQuery"]}.

size.description: Number of parent entities to return. Default is 10, maximum is 50.

from.description: Offset for pagination. Default is 0. Use with 'size' to page through results.

k.description: Number of nearest neighbors to consider internally (KNN parameter). Higher values may improve result quality at the cost of latency. Default is 100.

threshold.description: Minimum similarity score threshold (0.0 to 1.0). Results below this score are excluded. Default is 0.0 (no filtering). Use higher values like 0.5 or 0.7 to get only highly relevant results.

examples.description: Find tables related to customer purchases
Find dashboards about revenue in BigQuery
High-confidence search for PII data
Find pipeline assets processing user events

tools.name: get_entity_details
tools.description: Reads detailed information about a specific entity. This is a read-only operation. Supports multiple identification forms: fully qualified name (preferred), entity UUID, entity link (<#E::type::fqn>), or name+service combination. Response is optimized for LLM context by excluding verbose metadata fields. IMPORTANT: Use the 'fullyQualifiedName' and 'entityType' values directly from search_metadata or semantic_search results — do not construct the FQN manually.

parameters.description: Use 'fullyQualifiedName' and 'entityType' from search results directly. Also supports id, entityLink, or name+service for flexible entity lookup.

entityType.description: Type of entity (e.g., table, dashboard, topic, pipeline). Use the 'entityType' value from search results. Required for all lookup forms.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the entity. IMPORTANT: Use the exact 'fullyQualifiedName' value from search_metadata or semantic_search results. Do not attempt to construct or modify the FQN.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search_metadata or semantic_search directly — the tool resolves it automatically. If both 'fqn' and 'fullyQualifiedName' are provided, 'fqn' takes precedence.

id.description: UUID of the entity. Use when you have the entity ID from a previous response or URL. The tool will look up the entity by ID.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>. Example: <#E::table::postgres.mydb.myschema.mytable>. The tool parses the link and resolves the entity.

name.description: Simple name of the entity (not fully qualified). Must be combined with 'service' (and optionally 'database', 'schema') to construct the FQN. Example: for a table, provide name, service, database, and schema.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' parameter. Example: 'postgres'.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' and 'service' for table/schema entities. Example: 'mydb'.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name', 'service', and 'database' for table entities. Example: 'myschema'.

tools.name: create_glossary_term
tools.description: Creates a new Glossary Term. Note that a glossary term must be part of a Glossary, so the glossary must be specified in the parameters. If you can't find the right glossary to use, respond back to the user to create a new Glossary first. Note that you can help the user to create the Glossary as well. If you don't find any Glossary that could be related, please list to the user the available Glossaries so users can choose if they want to create or reuse something. Also, note that glossary terms can be hierarchical: for example, a glossary term 'Accounts' can have a child term 'Credit Account', 'Savings Account', etc. So if you find any terms that can be related, it might make sense to create a new term as a child of an existing term.

glossary.description: Glossary in which the term belongs. This should be its fully qualified name.

parentTerm.description: Optional parent term for the new term. This should be its fully qualified name defined as <glossary>.<term>. If the Glossary Term has other parents, the Fully Qualified Name will be <glossary>.<parent>...<term>. If not provided, the term will be created at the root level of the glossary.

owners.description: Glossary Term owner. This could be an OpenMetadata User or Team. If you don't know who the owner is, you can leave this empty, but let the user know that they can add owners later.

reviewers.description: Glossary Term reviewers. These are OpenMetadata Users or Teams who will review and approve the glossary term. If reviewers are set, the term will go through an approval workflow (status will be Draft until approved). If you don't know who the reviewers should be, you can leave this empty.

tools.name: create_glossary
tools.description: Creates a new Glossary. A Glossary is a collection of terms that are used to define the business vocabulary of an organization. Typically, similar terms are grouped together in a Glossary. For example, a Glossary names 'Marketing' could contain terms like 'Campaign', 'Lead', 'Opportunity', etc.

owners.description: Glossary Term owner. This could be an OpenMetadata User or Team. If you don't know who the owner is, you can leave this empty, but let the user know that they can add owners later.

reviewers.description: Glossary Term owner. This could be an OpenMetadata User or Team. If you don't know who the owner is, you can leave this empty, but let the user know that they can add owners later.

mutuallyExclusive.description: Glossary terms that are direct children in this glossary are mutually exclusive. When mutually exclusive is `true` only one term can be used to tag an entity. When mutually exclusive is `false`, multiple terms from this group can be used to tag an entity. This is an important setting. If you are not sure, ask the user to clarify. If the user doesn't know, set it to `false`.

tools.name: patch_entity
tools.description: Modifies an entity using JSONPatch operations. Requires edit permissions or ownership of the entity. Beforehand the Entity should be validated by finding it and creating a proper patch. IMPORTANT field naming rules: all array/list fields use PLURAL names in the JSON body — use 'domains' (not 'domain'), 'owners' (not 'owner'), 'tags' (not 'tag'), 'reviewers' (not 'reviewer'). Domain values must be entity reference objects: {"id": "<uuid>", "type": "domain"}. Owner values must be entity reference objects: {"id": "<uuid>", "type": "user" or "team"}. To add a domain: [{"op": "add", "path": "/domains/0", "value": {"id": "<domain-id>", "type": "domain", "name": "<domain-name>"}}]. To replace description: [{"op": "add", "path": "/description", "value": "new description"}]. Always look up entity UUIDs using search or get tools before patching.

fqn.description: Fully Qualified Name of the Entity to be patched.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search tools directly. If both are provided, 'fqn' takes precedence.

id.description: UUID of the entity to patch. Alternative to fqn/fullyQualifiedName for entity identification.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>. Alternative identification form.

name.description: Simple name of the entity. Must be combined with 'service' (and optionally 'database', 'schema') to construct the FQN.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' parameter.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' and 'service' for table/schema entities.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name', 'service', and 'database' for table entities.

patch.description: JSONPatch operations as a JSON array string. Each operation has 'op' (add/remove/replace), 'path' (JSON Pointer starting with /), and 'value'. Field paths MUST use plural names for array fields: /domains, /owners, /tags, /reviewers. Example to set a domain: [{"op": "add", "path": "/domains/0", "value": {"id": "<domain-uuid>", "type": "domain", "name": "<domain-name>"}}].

tools.name: get_entity_lineage
tools.description: Get detailed information about lineage (upstream/downstream dependencies) of a specific entity. Supports multiple identification forms: fully qualified name (preferred), entity UUID, entity link (<#E::type::fqn>), or name+service combination. Use this for root cause (upstream entities) or impact (downstream entities) analysis and explaining dependencies between entities.

parameters.description: Identify the entity using fqn, fullyQualifiedName, id, entityLink, or name+service. Entity type is required.

entityType.description: Type of entity (e.g., table, topic, pipeline). Required for all lookup forms.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the entity.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search tools directly. If both are provided, 'fqn' takes precedence.

id.description: UUID of the entity. Use when you have the entity ID from a previous response or URL.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>. Example: <#E::table::postgres.mydb.myschema.mytable>.

name.description: Simple name of the entity (not fully qualified). Must be combined with 'service' (and optionally 'database', 'schema') to construct the FQN.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' parameter.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' and 'service' for table/schema entities.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name', 'service', and 'database' for table entities.

upstreamDepth.description: Number of upstream hops to traverse. Default is 3, maximum is 10. Set to 0 to disable upstream traversal (downstream-only query).

downstreamDepth.description: Number of downstream hops to traverse. Default is 3, maximum is 10. Set to 0 to disable downstream traversal (upstream-only query).

tools.name: create_lineage
tools.description: This tool can be used to create lineage between two assets. It takes the source and target asset details and creates a lineage relationship between them.

parameters.description: Required to create lineage between two assets.

tools.name: get_test_definitions
tools.description: This tool can be used to get all the test definitions in the OpenMetadata. It returns a list of test definitions. These test definition can be used to create a test case for a table or a table's column. While creating column test for entity, column data type should be in supportedDataTypes of parameterDefinition.

parameters.description: These test definition are required to create a test case for table or a table's column.

entityType.description: Entity Type can be 'TABLE' for table asset/entity or 'COLUMN' for column level tests. Default is TABLE.

testPlatform.description: Default value can be 'OpenMetadata'. Other Platform can be 'OpenMetadata','GreatExpectations', 'DBT', 'Deequ', 'Soda', 'Other' if the user specifically gives the platform name.

after.description: This can be used to paginate the results. In the response you will get a nextCursor value, which can be used to get the next set of results. For the first call, this should be ignored.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default is 10.

tools.name: create_test_case
tools.description: This tool can be used to create a test case for a table or a table's column. It needs test definitions. These test definition can be found using the get_test_definitions tool. Supports multiple entity identification forms: fully qualified name (preferred), entity UUID, entity link (<#E::type::fqn>), or name+service combination. If this fails do not do other operations.

parameters.description: Identify the entity using fqn, fullyQualifiedName, id, entityLink, or name+service. Requires the test definition and the entity (table or column) to be tested.

name.description: Name of the test case. Either the user tells the name or auto generate a name based on the test definition and entity fqn.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the table for which the test case is being added. Always use the table FQN, not the column FQN.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search tools directly. If both are provided, 'fqn' takes precedence.

id.description: UUID of the entity. Use when you have the entity ID from a previous response.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>. Example: <#E::table::postgres.mydb.myschema.mytable>.

columnName.description: Name of the column to test. Required for column-level test definitions (entityType=COLUMN). This is just the column name, not the full FQN. For example, 'shop_id' not the full table.column path.

entityType.description: Type of the entity for which the test case is being added. Default is 'table'. It can only be one of these values 'container', 'workflowDefinition', 'testSuite', 'pipelineService', 'messagingService', 'type', 'dataContract', 'metadataService', 'appMarketPlaceDefinition', 'tag', 'dashboard', 'app', 'dataProduct', 'persona', 'workflow', 'kpi', 'apiService', 'query', 'searchIndex', 'classification', 'dashboardDataModel', 'glossary', 'apiEndpoint', 'storageService', 'domain', 'topic', 'databaseSchema', 'role', 'dataInsightChart', 'bot', 'mlmodelService', 'document', 'ingestionPipeline', 'database', 'searchService', 'testConnectionDefinition', 'webAnalyticEvent', 'table', 'policy', 'storedProcedure', 'databaseService', 'eventsubscription', 'dashboardService', 'apiCollection', 'team', 'mlmodel', 'glossaryTerm', 'pipeline', 'dataInsightCustomChart', 'metric', 'report', 'chart', 'user', 'testCase', 'testDefinition'.

testDefinitionName.description: Fully qualified name of the test definition to be used for the test case.

description.description: Description of the test case. This can be auto generated based on entity details, the test definition and type of test.

parameterValues.description: Parameter values for the test case. This is an array of objects, where each object contains the parameter name (this is 'name' from parameter definition in test definition) and value (can be asked from user or auto supplied). These parameter can be found from the testDefinitions from `parameterDefinition` which has name, description, dataType and whether it is required mandatorily.

items.description: Parameter values that can be passed for a Test Case.

name.description: Name of the parameter. Must match the parameter names in testCaseParameterDefinition

value.description: value to be passed for the Parameters. These are input from Users. We capture this in string and convert during the runtime.

tools.name: create_metric
tools.description: Creates a new Metric entity in OpenMetadata. A Metric represents a measurable business or technical KPI (e.g. daily revenue, error rate). Use this to register new metrics with optional expression, type, granularity, and unit of measurement. Metric can be expressed in SQL, Python, Java, or JavaScript.

name.description: Name of the metric. Must be unique and must not contain '::'.

description.description: Description of the metric in Markdown format.

displayName.description: Human-readable display name for the metric.

metricExpressionLanguage.description: Language used to define the metric expression.

metricExpressionCode.description: The code or query that computes the metric value (e.g. a SQL SELECT statement).

granularity.description: Time granularity at which the metric is computed.

unitOfMeasurement.description: Unit of measurement for the metric value.

customUnitOfMeasurement.description: Custom unit of measurement string. Required only when unitOfMeasurement is 'OTHER'.

owners.description: List of OpenMetadata usernames or team names to set as owners of this metric.

reviewers.description: List of OpenMetadata usernames or team names to set as reviewers of this metric.

relatedMetrics.description: Fully qualified names of related metrics (e.g. 'DailyRevenue', 'WeeklyRevenue').

tags.description: Tag FQNs to apply to this metric (e.g. 'Tier.Tier1', 'PII.Sensitive').

domains.description: Fully qualified names of the domains this metric belongs to (e.g. 'Finance', 'Marketing'). Assigns the metric to a domain for governance and access control.

tools.name: change_impact
tools.description: Analyzes the downstream impact of a proposed change to a data asset. Answers 'what breaks if I change X?' in one call by composing lineage traversal, dashboard/pipeline search, test case discovery, and policy attachment. Returns severity (critical/high/medium/low), affected asset lists, counts, and a Markdown narrative. This is a read-only analysis tool — it does not modify any entities.

parameters.description: Identify the entity using fqn, fullyQualifiedName, id, entityLink, or name+service. Specify the proposed change kind and details.

entityType.description: Type of entity (e.g., table, dashboard, topic, pipeline). Default is 'table'. Required for all lookup forms.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the entity to analyze.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search tools directly. If both are provided, 'fqn' takes precedence.

id.description: UUID of the entity. Alternative to fqn/fullyQualifiedName for entity identification.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>. Alternative identification form.

name.description: Simple name of the entity. Must be combined with 'service' (and optionally 'database', 'schema') to construct the FQN.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' parameter.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' and 'service'.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name', 'service', and 'database'.

proposedChange.description: Describes the proposed change. Required. Supported kinds: 'dropColumn' (requires column), 'changeColumnType' (requires column, fromType, toType), 'deprecateEntity', 'custom' (requires description). Example: {"kind": "dropColumn", "column": "customer_id"}

kind.description: Type of proposed change. One of: dropColumn, changeColumnType, deprecateEntity, custom.

column.description: Column name affected by the change. Required for dropColumn and changeColumnType kinds.

fromType.description: Current data type of the column. Required for changeColumnType kind.

toType.description: New data type for the column. Required for changeColumnType kind.

description.description: Free-text description of the change. Required for custom kind.

downstreamDepth.description: Number of downstream hops to traverse for impact analysis. Default is 3, maximum is 10. Higher values give broader impact visibility but take longer.

includeDashboards.description: Whether to include dashboards and pipelines that reference the affected entity/column. Default is true.

includeTests.description: Whether to include test cases that touch the affected entity/column. Default is true.

includePolicies.description: Whether to include policies attached to the affected entity/domain. Default is true.

tools.name: incident_timeline
tools.description: Builds a chronological incident timeline for a data asset, composing root cause analysis, ChangeEvent feed, test case result history, and ownership resolution into a Slack/PagerDuty-ready Markdown narrative. Answers 'what happened and who owns it?' in one call. Returns a timeline of events (upstream failures, schema changes, test failures/recoveries), root cause, suggested owners, and an optional Markdown narrative. This is a read-only analysis tool — it does not modify any entities.

parameters.description: Identify the entity using fqn, fullyQualifiedName, id, entityLink, or name+service. Optionally specify lookback window and output format.

entityType.description: Type of entity (e.g., table, dashboard, topic, pipeline). Default is 'table'. Required for all lookup forms.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the entity.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search tools directly. If both are provided, 'fqn' takes precedence.

id.description: UUID of the entity. Alternative to fqn/fullyQualifiedName for entity identification.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>. Alternative identification form.

name.description: Simple name of the entity. Must be combined with 'service' (and optionally 'database', 'schema') to construct the FQN.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' parameter.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name' and 'service'.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction. Used with 'name', 'service', and 'database'.

lookbackHours.description: Lookback window in hours for event retrieval. Default is 72 (3 days), maximum is 720 (30 days).

format.description: Output format for the narrative. 'markdown' produces a Markdown narrative (default). 'json' omits the narrative and returns structured data only.

tools.name: find_unowned_assets
tools.description: Finds data assets without owners, ranked by downstream impact. Use this to identify governance gaps and prioritize ownership assignment. Returns a prioritized list where assets with more downstream dependencies rank higher (higher impact if unowned). Supports optional scope filtering by domain or service. Rate-limited: one call per user per 5-minute window (returns 429 if exceeded). After reviewing the list, use `suggest_owner_for` to identify the best owner candidate for each unowned asset, then `draft_ownership_patch` to prepare the ownership assignment for review. This is a read-only tool — it does not modify any entities.

parameters.description: Optionally filter by scope (domain/service) and entity type. Default finds unowned tables.

entityType.description: Type of entity to search for unowned assets. Default is 'table'.

oneOf.description: Domain name to scope the search (shorthand for domain scope).
Scope filter with explicit type and value.

scope.description: Optional scope filter. Pass a domain name string (shorthand) or {type, value} object.

limit.description: Maximum number of unowned assets to return. Default is 25, maximum is 200.

examples.description: Find unowned tables across the catalog
Find unowned tables in the Marketing domain
Find unowned dashboards in BigQuery service

tools.name: suggest_owner_for
tools.description: Suggests the best owner candidates for a specific unowned data asset. Uses weighted scoring: 3× most frequent recent patcher (last 90 days), 2× owners of upstream entities, 1× domain default owner, 1× owners of sibling tables in the same schema. Returns top-3 candidates with scores and rationale. After choosing a candidate, use `draft_ownership_patch` to generate a review-ready JSONPatch. This is a read-only tool — it does not modify any entities.

parameters.description: Identify the entity using fqn, fullyQualifiedName, id, entityLink, or name+service.

entityType.description: Type of entity (e.g., table, dashboard). Default is 'table'.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the entity.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Alias for 'fqn'. Accepts the 'fullyQualifiedName' value returned by search tools directly.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>.

name.description: Simple name of the entity. Must be combined with 'service'.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction.

examples.description: Suggest owner for a specific table
Suggest owner using fullyQualifiedName from search results

tools.name: draft_ownership_patch
tools.description: Drafts a JSONPatch for assigning ownership to an entity. Returns the patch for human or agent review — does NOT apply it. The consumer must explicitly call `patch_entity` to apply. Supports 'add' mode (append owner to existing) and 'replace' mode (overwrite all owners). Use this after `suggest_owner_for` identifies the best candidate. This is a safe, non-mutating tool.

parameters.description: Identify the entity and specify the owner to assign. The owner can be a user or team.

fqn.description: Fully qualified name of the entity.

entityLink.description: OpenMetadata entity link in Markdown format: <#E::entityType::fqn>.

name.description: Simple name of the entity. Must be combined with 'service'.

service.description: Service name for composite FQN construction.

database.description: Database name for composite FQN construction.

schema.description: Schema name for composite FQN construction.

oneOf.description: Owner name (assumed to be a user).
Owner specification with name, type, and optional id.

name.description: Name of the user or team to assign as owner.

id.description: UUID of the owner entity. If not provided, the tool will resolve by name.

owner.description: Owner to assign. Provide a name string (shorthand for user) or {name, type?, id?} object.

mode.description: Patch mode. 'add' appends the owner to existing owners (default). 'replace' overwrites all existing owners — use with caution.

examples.description: Draft patch to add a user as owner

tools.name: scan_governance_coverage
tools.description: Reports what percentage of data assets have key governance attributes populated (owner, tier, domain, description, PII tags). Use this to identify governance gaps and prioritize remediation. Returns coverage percentages per attribute, gap details with top-offending entities, and PII candidate detection (columns matching PII name patterns that lack PII tags). Supports optional scope filtering by domain or service. After reviewing the report, use `find_unowned_assets` to prioritize ownership assignment, `suggest_owner_for` to identify owners, and `draft_ownership_patch` to prepare ownership patches. For PII candidates, use `patch_entity` to apply PII tags. This is a read-only tool — it does not modify any entities.

parameters.description: Optionally filter by scope (domain/service) and entity type. Default scans tables.

entityType.description: Type of entity to scan for governance coverage. Default is 'table'. Other options: 'dashboard', 'topic', 'pipeline', 'mlmodel', 'container'.

oneOf.description: Domain name to scope the scan (shorthand for domain scope).
Scope filter with explicit type and value.

scope.description: Optional scope filter. Pass a domain name string (shorthand) or {type, value} object.

examples.description: Scan governance coverage across all tables
Scan governance coverage for the Marketing domain
Scan governance coverage for BigQuery service
Scan governance coverage for dashboards

tools.name: root_cause_analysis
tools.description: Performs comprehensive root cause analysis via data quality lineage. Supports multiple entity identification forms: fully qualified name (preferred), entity UUID, entity link (<#E::type::fqn>), or name+service combination. First identifies upstream failures that may be causing issues for the specified asset. If failures are found, automatically analyzes downstream impact to show which assets may be affected. Returns both upstream root causes and downstream impact analysis in a structured envelope. In the response 'status' indicates whether upstream failures were found. If 'status' is 'failed', the 'upstreamAnalysis' can be used to identify the nodes and edges leading to failures and downstreamAnalysis can tell what all nodes in downstream are impacted. If 'status' is 'success', it means no upstream failures were found, and downstream impact analysis was not performed. Failed test case results are capped at 5 per suite (maxTestCaseResultsPerSuite) to control context size; set 'truncated: true' in the response if more exist.

tools.name: validate_patch
tools.description: Previews the effect of a JSON Patch without applying it. Accepts the same inputs as `patch_entity` but returns {beforeSnapshot, afterSnapshot, diff, affectedDownstreamCount, affectedDownstreamCountNote, warnings[]} without mutating any state. Use this to review changes before calling `patch_entity` to apply them. The `diff` field shows RFC 6902 JSON Patch operations that represent the difference between before and after snapshots. The `affectedDownstreamCount` is capped at 1-hop lineage and is NOT exhaustive — the `affectedDownstreamCountNote` field reminds consumers to use `change_impact` for full blast-radius analysis. Warnings flag semantically risky changes: ownerRemoval (removing all owners), tierRemoval (removing tier), massTagRemoval (removing ≥5 tags), descriptionCleared (clearing the description). This is a read-only, non-mutating tool.

tools.name: generate_data_contract
tools.description: Exports a data contract YAML from a table entity. The contract captures the current state of the entity including schema (columns), owners, tier, tags, glossary terms, domains, and optional fields like retentionPeriod, sourceUrl, and schemaDefinition. The contract uses apiVersion: openmetadata.org/v1alpha1 and is designed for Git version control. Use `apply_data_contract` to re-import an edited contract. This is a read-only, non-mutating tool.

tools.name: apply_data_contract
tools.description: Applies a data contract YAML to bring a catalog entity into conformance with the contract. Computes the JSON Patch operations needed, previews the diff (dryRun=true, default), or applies the changes with atomic rollback on failure (dryRun=false). By default, dryRun=true returns a preview with a validate_patch-style diff showing before/after snapshots, warnings, and affected downstream count. Set dryRun=false to apply the patch. The contract must contain metadata.fqn identifying the target entity. If the entity does not exist, set createIfMissing=true to signal intent (automatic creation is deferred). The patch is atomic: either all changes apply or none do, so no inconsistent catalog state is possible. Schema: apiVersion: openmetadata.org/v1alpha1.

contractYaml.description: The data contract YAML string (as produced by generate_data_contract). Must contain metadata.fqn identifying the target entity.

entityType.description: Type of entity (default: 'table'). Must match the entity referenced in the contract.

dryRun.description: If true (default), returns a preview of changes without applying them. If false, applies the changes to the catalog.

createIfMissing.description: If true, allows creating entities referenced by the contract that don't exist yet. If false (default), throws an error when the entity is not found.

tools.name: lineage_from_sql
tools.description: Parses raw SQL and produces lineage edge proposals between catalog entities. Extracts source and target table references from SQL using JSQLParser, resolves each table against the OpenMetadata catalog, and assigns a confidence score. Supported SQL shapes: SELECT FROM, INSERT INTO SELECT, CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW AS, plus CTE inlining. Default apply=false returns a plan of proposed lineage edges without creating them. Set apply=true to create lineage edges for high-confidence matches (confidence ≥ 0.8); low-confidence edges are returned under requiresConfirmation for manual review. Rejects SQL exceeding 4000 characters or with unparseable syntax. This tool bridges the gap between SQL snippets (dbt models, Airflow tasks, notebooks) and the catalog's lineage graph.

sql.description: Raw SQL string to parse for lineage extraction. Maximum length is 4000 characters. Supports SELECT, INSERT INTO SELECT, CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, CREATE/ALTER VIEW, and CTE (WITH) constructs.

defaultService.description: Default database service name for table resolution. When table names in SQL lack a service prefix, this service is used to construct candidate FQNs (e.g., 'postgres'). Improves confidence scores by narrowing the search scope.

apply.description: If true, creates lineage edges for all resolved tables with confidence ≥ 0.8. Low-confidence edges are returned under requiresConfirmation. If false (default), returns the plan without creating any edges.

examples.description: Extract lineage from a dbt model SQL
examples.sql: CREATE TABLE orders_summary AS SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

tools.name: suggest_test_cases
tools.description: Proposes test cases for a table based on its schema, constraints, profiler data, and lineage. Generates suggestions for: columnValuesToBeNotNull (PK/NOT_NULL columns), columnValuesToBeUnique (PK columns), tableRowCountToBeBetween (profiler ±3σ), tableFreshness (update cadence), and referential integrity (FK constraints). Each proposal includes testDefinitionFqn, parameters, rationale, and confidence. Does NOT apply proposals — use create_test_case to apply explicitly.

tools.name: rank_assets_by_cost
tools.description: Ranks data assets by cost × freshness (staleness) priority score. Uses usage percentile rank, storage size, and time since last update to identify expensive, stale tables wasting money. Returns top-N ranked assets with costScore, stalenessScore, and priorityScore. Tables missing usage or size data are listed under 'insufficientSignal' (never silently dropped). Supports optional scope filtering by domain or service, minStalenessDays filter, and configurable limit. Scoring formula: priorityScore = costScore × (1 + stalenessScore), where costScore = usageRank × (1 + sizeWeight) and stalenessScore = min(daysSinceUpdate / 30, 5.0) / 5.0. Rate-limited to one call per user per 5 minutes. This is a read-only tool — it does not modify any entities.

parameters.description: Optionally filter by scope (domain/service), minimum staleness days, and limit. Default ranks tables by cost × freshness.

entityType.description: Type of entity to rank. Default is 'table'. Other options: 'dashboard', 'topic', 'pipeline', 'mlmodel', 'container'.

oneOf.description: Domain name to scope the ranking (shorthand for domain scope).
Scope filter with explicit type and value.

scope.description: Optional scope filter. Pass a domain name string (shorthand) or {type, value} object.

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked assets to return. Default is 25, maximum is 200.

minStalenessDays.description: Minimum days since last update to include in ranking. Default is 0 (include all). Use this to focus on stale assets (e.g., minStalenessDays=30 for assets not updated in 30+ days).
